content.text: Venezuelan creators face a critical infrastructure gap: no access to Stripe, PayPal, or conventional payment processors. This is not a temporary restriction—it's a permanent exclusion from the platforms that power global digital commerce. The solution is not a workaround but a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/complete-deep-dive-how-bangladeshi-freelancers-accept-international-3|complete]] re-architecture of your payment stack. This post outlines the exact steps to deploy a sovereign commerce infrastructure that accepts [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payments-tanzanian-online-sellers-which-architecture-actually-3|COREMERCH guide to crypto]]-payments-tanzanian-online-sellers-minimum-viable-stack|Crypto Payments]] payments from anywhere, using tools you fully own and control. No subscriptions. No platform lock-in. Built to withstand the same financial isolation that COREMERCH was pressure-tested against in Zimbabwe.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: The Full List With Context

1. **Host on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages**—Both are free, globally distributed, and require no server management. GitHub Pages uses Jekyll for static sites, while Cloudflare Pages supports modern frameworks like React or Vue. 2. **Use Cloudflare Workers for backend logic**—Write serverless functions in JavaScript to handle order processing, payment verification, and file delivery. Costs $0 unless you scale beyond 10 million requests/month. 3. **Store orders in Supabase or Google Sheets**—Supabase is a free Postgres database with built-in auth and API access. Google Sheets is simpler but requires Apps Script for automation. 4. **Deliver files via Google Drive or Cloudflare R2**—Google Drive is free up to 15GB. Cloudflare R2 charges $0.015/GB for storage and $0.01/GB for egress. 5. **Integrate NOWPayments for crypto processing**—Supports 300+ cryptocurrencies with a 0.5% fee. No KYC. No buyer account required. Use USDT on Tron for under $0.10 fees and under 60-second settlement.
Why Each Item on This List Matters

GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages eliminate hosting costs and ensure your store loads fast globally. Cloudflare Workers provide backend logic without managing servers, critical for automating payment verification and file delivery. Supabase or Google Sheets store order data in a format you control, unlike SaaS platforms that lock you in. Google Drive and Cloudflare R2 offer scalable file storage with predictable pricing. NOWPayments removes the need for a payment processor account, letting buyers pay directly from their crypto wallets. Each tool is selected for its cost, speed, and sovereignty—no single point of failure, no platform dependency.
The Ones Most Creators Get Wrong

Most creators attempt to build their own payment verification system, which fails under real-world transaction volume. NOWPayments handles this with webhooks that fire the moment payment confirms on-chain. Another mistake is using centralized file storage like AWS S3 without redundancy—Cloudflare R2 is cheaper and integrates natively with Workers. Finally, relying on a single hosting provider creates a single point of failure. GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages are both free, but deploying to both ensures uptime even if one service degrades.
USDT on Tron settles in under 60 seconds for under $0.10—ideal for low-value digital products.
How to Prioritise What to Implement First

Start with hosting and payment processing—deploy your store to GitHub Pages and integrate NOWPayments first. Without these, you cannot accept payments. Next, add backend logic with Cloudflare Workers to automate order fulfillment. Then, configure file storage with Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Finally, set up order storage in Supabase or Google Sheets. Prioritize tools that directly generate revenue, then layer in data storage and redundancy. The Complete Builder Kit ($197) provides all blueprints and templates to deploy this stack in 48 hours.
Putting the List Into a Deployable Stack

Deploy Stack 02 (Edge Commerce Stack) for a fully integrated solution. Cloudflare Pages hosts your store, Workers handle backend logic, Supabase stores orders, and NOWPayments processes crypto. This stack includes SPF/DKIM/DMARC email configuration for order receipts and end-to-end testing. COREMERCH deploys this stack for you in 48 hours, or you can build it yourself using the Complete Builder Kit ($197). Every component is open-source, and you own the entire infrastructure after deployment. No subscriptions. No platform lock-in. Built to operate in environments where conventional payment processors are permanently unavailable.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

Creators in Africa can sell digital products to international buyers by deploying a sovereign commerce stack that accepts crypto payments. Use GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend logic, and NOWPayments for crypto processing. Binance P2P allows buyers to convert local currencies like naira, cedis, or Kenyan shillings into USDT, which settles in under 60 seconds for under $0.10 on the Tron network. This infrastructure removes geographic payment barriers entirely, letting you sell to anyone with a crypto wallet.
Binance P2P supports fiat-to-crypto conversions in Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, and Pakistan.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

To sell ebooks in Nigeria without PayPal, or digital products in Ghana with crypto payments, the same infrastructure applies. The Complete Builder Kit ($197) includes all blueprints and templates to deploy these stacks, available for instant download at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. Whether you're in Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Venezuela, the tools are the same—what changes is how you configure them for your local context. Binance P2P supports fiat-to-crypto conversions in all these regions, making USDT on Tron the ideal settlement currency.
Your Deployment Checklist

1. Deploy your store to GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. 2. Write a Cloudflare Worker to handle payment verification via NOWPayments webhooks. 3. Set up order storage in Supabase or Google Sheets. 4. Configure file delivery from Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. 5. Test end-to-end: Place a test order using USDT on Tron, verify the webhook fires, and confirm file delivery. 6. Add SPF/DKIM/DMARC records to your domain for secure order emails. 7. Scale by adding more products and monitoring transaction fees—use Binance P2P for local fiat-to-crypto conversions.
Frequently Asked Questions
Can I use this stack if I’m not technical?
Yes. The Sovereign Starter Stack ($97) deploys GitHub Pages + Apps Script + NOWPayments for you in 48 hours. Includes 3 products loaded and 30-day support.
What if my buyers don’t have crypto?
Binance P2P supports naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees. Buyers can convert local currency to USDT and pay you directly.
How do I handle refunds?
Issue a new USDT transaction from your wallet to the buyer’s address. NOWPayments does not handle refunds—you control the process directly.
Is this legal in Venezuela?
Yes. Crypto transactions are legal in Venezuela, and this stack does not rely on any restricted platforms. You own the infrastructure.
What if Cloudflare or GitHub goes down?
Deploy to both GitHub Pages and Cloudflare Pages for redundancy. If one service degrades, your store remains live on the other.
